description: A real single-node Raft cluster is started with one FSM value that implements FSM, BatchingFSM, and ConfigurationStore. The harness waits for the bootstrap LogConfiguration entry to be committed and applied, then observes whether ApplyBatch received that committed configuration entry and whether StoreConfiguration was invoked.

harness.description: Start a real in-memory Raft cluster with a combined FSM, commit the bootstrap configuration entry, and count configuration deliveries through ApplyBatch and StoreConfiguration.
semantic_changes: Uses the real BootstrapCluster, NewRaft, runFSM, and Barrier paths.
The single FSM value implements FSM, BatchingFSM, and ConfigurationStore so the batch branch is selected while the configuration-store callback is applicable.
The harness only counts LogConfiguration entries in ApplyBatch and invocations of StoreConfiguration; it does not replace protocol logic.

legality.derivation: ConfigurationStore states that StoreConfiguration is invoked once a log entry containing a configuration change is committed. BatchingFSM states that ApplyBatch receives committed log entries and that LogConfiguration is presently among the types sent. runFSM selects the batch branch whenever the FSM implements BatchingFSM, and that branch sends LogConfiguration to ApplyBatch without calling the already-detected configStore. The callback contract is therefore not met for a single FSM value implementing both optional interfaces.
legality.applicability: The same FSM value implements ConfigurationStore and BatchingFSM, and a committed LogConfiguration entry is applied through runFSM's batching branch.
unresolved: The check observes the bootstrap configuration entry in one single-node cluster; it does not enumerate every configuration-change command or every durable FSM implementation.
conflicts: The batching branch intentionally routes LogConfiguration to ApplyBatch, but the ConfigurationStore contract independently requires StoreConfiguration for the committed configuration entry.
alternatives: An FSM that does not implement ConfigurationStore is outside this obligation.

grounding.derivation: The result event reports whether a committed configuration entry was observed in ApplyBatch and the observed number of StoreConfiguration invocations for the same FSM identity.
grounding.applicability: Applies when one FSM value implements both BatchingFSM and ConfigurationStore and a committed LogConfiguration entry is applied.

observable_properties.description: If a committed configuration entry is delivered to a combined FSM through ApplyBatch, ConfigurationStore requires StoreConfiguration to have been invoked for that committed entry.

uncertainties: The check uses the bootstrap configuration entry in a single-node cluster rather than every configuration-change command.
The check does not establish whether a particular application has an independent configuration-recovery mechanism outside ConfigurationStore.
